[LLM] sanitize-html xmp-tag XSS payload (CVE-2026-44990) in inbound HTTP request Exploitation Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP requests carrying the CVE-2026-44990 sanitize-html bypass signature: an <xmp> element wrapping a <script> tag or HTML event handler (onerror=/onload=/onclick=). The xmp+script joint signature is the literal PoC from the GHSA-rpr9-rxv7-x643 advisory and is essentially never benign user content, so the URI/body match is high-fidelity for exploitation attempts against Apostrophe CMS or any other consumer of sanitize-html <=2.17.3. Rationale: The advisory's PoC is literal: `<xmp><script>alert(1)</script></xmp>`, `<xmp><img src=x onerror=alert(1)></xmp>`, `<xmp><svg><script>alert(1)</script></svg></xmp>`. Co-occurrence of <xmp> with <script> or an on*= handler in a single request URI/query is the exact bypass signature and effectively never appears in legitimate user-submitted content — even rich-text editors do not emit xmp. Coverage caveat: most stored-XSS exploitation comes via POST bodies, which aren't carried in DeviceNetworkEvents or standard IIS logs, hence Medium confidence overall; WAFs that mirror the body into CEF Message give the strongest signal. Cross-checked the related ApostropheCMS sanitize-html GHSA family (GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm / CVE-2026-40186 — the textarea/option entity-decode bypass — confirms the same `nonTextTags`/`ontext` raw-text passthrough pattern at the root of this CVE). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/apostrophecms/sanitize-html/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md • https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm • https://github.com/apostrophecms/sanitize-html
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Note: covers ONLY URL/query-string reflection. POST bodies are not captured in DeviceNetworkEvents.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess", "HttpConnectionInspected", "InboundConnectionAccepted")
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl contains "xmp"
| where (RemoteUrl contains "<xmp>" or RemoteUrl contains "<XMP>" or RemoteUrl contains "%3cxmp%3e" or RemoteUrl contains "%3CXMP%3E")
| where (RemoteUrl contains "<script" or RemoteUrl contains "%3cscript" or RemoteUrl contains "%3Cscript" or RemoteUrl contains "onerror=" or RemoteUrl contains "onload=" or RemoteUrl contains "onclick=" or RemoteUrl contains "onerror%3d" or RemoteUrl contains "onload%3d")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
// IIS access logs + WAF/CEF — covers URL query and request body excerpts (where carried by the WAF).
let _xmp_url = (s:string) { s contains "<xmp>" or s contains "<XMP>" or s contains "%3cxmp%3e" or s contains "%3CXMP%3E" or s contains "%3cXmp%3e" };
let _xss_url = (s:string) { s contains "<script" or s contains "%3cscript" or s contains "%3Cscript" or s contains "onerror=" or s contains "onload=" or s contains "onclick=" or s contains "onmouseover=" or s contains "onerror%3d" or s contains "onload%3d" };
union isfuzzy=true
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
  | where _xmp_url(csUriQuery) or _xmp_url(csUriStem)
  | where _xss_url(csUriQuery) or _xss_url(csUriStem)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
  | where _xmp_url(RequestURL) or _xmp_url(Message)
  | where _xss_url(RequestURL) or _xss_url(Message)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct), Computer=DestinationHostName, cIP=SourceIP, csMethod=RequestMethod, csUriStem=RequestURL, csUriQuery=tostring(Message), scStatus=tostring(EventOutcome), csUserAgent=RequestClientApplication
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Vulnerable sanitize-html <=2.17.3 / Apostrophe CMS asset inventory (CVE-2026-44990) Reconnaissance High
Identifies hosts running a vulnerable build of sanitize-html or Apostrophe CMS as reported by Defender TVM. The hunt closes the exposure window by producing a patch list before exploitation telemetry appears, and gives the SOC a target asset set for tighter monitoring of UC#1. Rationale: The advisory pins affected to npm:sanitize-html <=2.17.3 (PoC against 2.17.3); upstream changelog and the related GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm advisory show the fix line continues in the 2.17.x branch. Hunting both via TVM CveId (when MS finishes ingesting the CVE feed) and via raw `SoftwareName + SoftwareVersion` catches the gap where the CVE lookup hasn't propagated yet. TVM data is asset-level so FP is essentially zero — output is a patch list, not an alert. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/apostrophecms/sanitize-html/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md • https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm
ATT&CKT1190

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

[LLM] Talos weekly top-prevalent malware hash watch (Coinminer / Injector / W32.Variant) Installation High
Surfaces any execution, image-load, or file-write of the four SHA256/MD5 hashes Cisco Talos published in the 2026-05-14 Threat Source newsletter as the most prevalent malware seen in Talos telemetry that week (Win.Worm.Coinminer VID001.exe, W32.Injector d4aa3e70…_63_Exe.exe, W32.Variant u112417.dat, Auto.90B145 APQ9305.dll). Article-specific because it pins on the exact SHA256/MD5 + Talos detection names from this week's bulletin, not a generic IOC sweep. Rationale: Hash IOCs are deterministic — these four SHA256s and the four MD5s come straight from Cisco Talos's weekly telemetry top-list with named verdicts (Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201, W32.Injector:Gen.21ie.1201, W32.Variant:MalwareXgenMisc.29d4.1201, Auto.90B145.282358.in02). They were corroborated by following each Talos file-reputation URL embedded in the article (talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=<SHA256>) which is Talos's authoritative reputation service confirming the verdict. The example filenames VID001.exe / u112417.dat / APQ9305.dll are renameable and only used as soft secondary signal in Splunk — the SHA256/MD5 are the high-fidelity anchors. FP rate is low because we're hash-pinned; the only realistic FPs are authorized malware sandbox hosts (allowlist them). Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-time-of-much-patching-is-coming/ • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Portainer Swarm service create/update API access (CVE-2026-44849 exploitation path) Exploitation Medium
Hunts for HTTP POST traffic to the Portainer Docker Swarm service create / update endpoints that the CVE-2026-44849 advisory identifies as the bypass surface. Surfaces the specific URI paths (/services/create and /services/{id}/update) that skip EndpointSecuritySettings validation so analysts can pivot to who exercised them and from where. Rationale: Targets the two URIs the GHSA explicitly names as the bypass surface (POST /services/create with 1-of-7 checks, POST /services/{id}/update with 0-of-7 checks, plus POST /volumes/create which never had the bind-mount check). Pivots on the exact paths from the advisory so signal is bound to the vulnerable endpoints rather than generic Docker API noise. Cross-referenced with Portainer release notes (2.33.8 / 2.39.2 / 2.41.0). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/portainer/portainer/releases • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/services/create", "/volumes/create")
   or RemoteUrl matches regex @"/services/[^/]+/update"
| where RemotePort in (9000, 9443, 8000, 443)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hits = count(), AnyCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl
| order by LastSeen desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod =~ "POST"
| where csUriStem has_any ("/services/create", "/volumes/create")
   or csUriStem matches regex @"/services/[^/]+/update"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count(), Methods = make_set(csMethod), URIs = make_set(csUriStem)
           by Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName, csUserAgent
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] Portainer Swarm service spec with elevated Linux capabilities or unconfined Seccomp Exploitation High
Hunts for the docker daemon on a Swarm-enabled host receiving service specs that contain the privileged values the CVE-2026-44849 advisory describes (CapabilityAdd: SYS_ADMIN/NET_ADMIN/SYS_PTRACE/ALL, Privileges.Seccomp.Mode: unconfined, AppArmor disabled). Captures the daemon-side artefact of the bypass even when proxy logs don't include request bodies. Rationale: Pulls the exact capability strings (SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, ALL) and modes (unconfined Seccomp, disabled AppArmor) listed in the GHSA Impact section. These values are not part of normal container spec on most fleets, so the binding to dockerd/containerd/runc plus those specific tokens keeps FP rate low. Verified against the advisory's pre-fix code excerpt showing CapabilityAdd/Sysctls/Privileges were never parsed by the partial service struct. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/service/create/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1611 T1610 T1068

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
   or FileName in~ ("runc", "crun", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("CAP_SYS_ADMIN", "CAP_NET_ADMIN", "CAP_SYS_PTRACE", "cap_sys_admin", "cap_net_admin", "cap_sys_ptrace", "\"ALL\"", "seccomp=unconfined", "apparmor=unconfined", "AppArmorProfile=unconfined", "\"Mode\":\"unconfined\"")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

| where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "portainer", "runc", "crun")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("CAP_SYS_ADMIN", "CAP_NET_ADMIN", "CAP_SYS_PTRACE", "cap_sys_admin", "cap_net_admin", "cap_sys_ptrace", "seccomp=unconfined", "apparmor=unconfined", "\"unconfined\"", "\"capabilities\":[\"ALL\"]", "CapabilityAdd")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, HostIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Container escape via chroot/nsenter against mounted host filesystem Actions on Objectives High
Hunts for chroot or nsenter invocations targeting /host, /proc/1/ns, or /proc/1/root — the textbook second-stage of the CVE-2026-44849 chain where the attacker has already created/updated a Swarm service that bind-mounts the host root and now pivots into the host namespace. Targets the executable + flag combinations that distinguish escape from benign chroot use. Rationale: Bound to the specific escape pattern the GHSA describes: 'access the host filesystem from the running container (e.g. via chroot /host)'. Pairs the LOLBin (chroot/nsenter) with the namespace-target tokens so it doesn't match administrative chroot use, and excludes systemd/snapd parents that legitimately invoke chroot during host operations. The advisory text 'chroot /host' is used verbatim as one of the high-signal matches. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/ • https://gtfobins.github.io/gtfobins/chroot/
ATT&CKT1611 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("chroot", "nsenter")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/host", "/proc/1/ns", "/proc/1/root", "--target 1", "--target=1", "-t 1")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("init", "systemd", "snapd", "snap-confine", "docker-init", "tini")
| where AccountName != "root" or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2", "runc", "crun", "dockerd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessParentCreationTime
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in ("auth", "authpriv", "daemon", "user")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("chroot /host", "chroot=/host", "nsenter --target 1", "nsenter -t 1", "--mount=/proc/1/ns/mnt", "/proc/1/root", "chroot /proc/1/root")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, ProcessID, SyslogMessage, SeverityLevel, HostIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Container Escape via chroot or nsenter to Host Namespace
id: 3c5c9f9a-5f6e-4b6a-9c5a-44849aaa0003
description: Detects chroot or nsenter invoked against /host, /proc/1/ns, or PID-1 mount namespace — the canonical escape from a bind-mounted container.
references:

source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) @process.name:(chroot OR nsenter) (@process.command_line:(*/host* OR */proc/1/ns* OR */proc/1/root* OR *--target?1* OR *-t?1*)) -@process.parent.name:(systemd OR snapd OR snap-confine OR docker-init OR tini)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 
| ImageFileName=/\/(chroot|nsenter)$/i 
| regex("(/host|/proc/1/ns|/proc/1/root|--target[= ]1|-t 1)", field=CommandLine) 
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(systemd|snapd|snap-confine|docker-init|tini)$/i 
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

[LLM] Container start with docker.sock or sensitive host-path bind mount Exploitation High
Hunts for container processes whose runtime spec includes a bind mount of /var/run/docker.sock, /, /root/.ssh, or the Portainer data directory — the post-bypass artefacts of CVE-2026-44849 where a non-admin user has slipped an unrestricted bind mount past the missing AllowBindMountsForRegularUsers check. The docker.sock variant is particularly high-signal because it directly enables sibling-container escape. Rationale: Pulls the exact sensitive paths the advisory enumerates ('bind mounts of any host path, including /, /var/run/docker.sock, SSH keys, or Portainer's own database'). Each of those paths is named verbatim in the Impact section, making the match high-fidelity. docker.sock + a container is sufficient on its own to grant container-breakout primitives, so this also fires as a leading indicator even without confirmed exploitation of CVE-2026-44849. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1611 T1613 T1525
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
   or FileName in~ ("runc", "crun", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/var/run/docker.sock", "docker.sock", "-v /:", "--volume=/:", "source=/ ", "source=/,", "source=/var/run/docker.sock", "/root/.ssh", "/data/portainer", "/host/etc", "\"Source\":\"/\"")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "containerd-shim", "runc", "crun")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/var/run/docker.sock", "docker.sock", "-v /:", "--volume=/:", "source=/ ", "source=/,", "/root/.ssh", "/data/portainer", "\"Source\":\"/\"", "\"Source\":\"/var/run/docker.sock\"")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, HostIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Docker local-driver volume created with type=none and o=bind (CVE-2026-44849 volume variant) Exploitation High
Hunts for the volume-driver-bind bypass variant the advisory calls out separately: a Type:volume mount whose VolumeOptions.DriverConfig.Options declares the local driver with type=none and o=bind, or a direct POST /volumes/create with the same payload. Either path materialises a bind-equivalent mount that the partial Mounts struct check never inspected on any Portainer branch. Rationale: Targets the volume-driver-bind variant called out in its own paragraph of the advisory: 'A mount with Type:"volume" and VolumeOptions.DriverConfig.Options: {type:"none", o:"bind", device:"<host path>"} is forwarded to the Docker daemon unchanged'. The triple type=none + o=bind + device= is the canonical local-driver bind incantation; legitimate use of this combination is extremely rare outside of explicit infrastructure-as-code volume declarations on the same host. Also unions in POST /volumes/create on the proxy log because the advisory notes that endpoint never had the AllowBindMountsForRegularUsers check on any branch. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/volume/create/ • https://docs.docker.com/storage/volumes/
ATT&CKT1611 T1078.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd", "docker", "containerd") or FileName in~ ("docker", "dockerd")
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "type=none" and ProcessCommandLine has "o=bind" and ProcessCommandLine has "device=")
     or (ProcessCommandLine has "volume create" and ProcessCommandLine has "--driver local" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-o type=none", "--opt type=none"))
     or (ProcessCommandLine has "VolumeOptions" and ProcessCommandLine has "DriverConfig")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let DockerActivity = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "docker")
    | where (SyslogMessage has "type=none" and SyslogMessage has "o=bind")
         or (SyslogMessage has "\"type\":\"none\"" and SyslogMessage has "\"o\":\"bind\"")
         or (SyslogMessage has "DriverConfig" and SyslogMessage has "\"local\"" and SyslogMessage has "device");
let WebActivity = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriStem has "/volumes/create" or csUriStem matches regex @"/services/[^/]+/(create|update)"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUserName, csUriStem, csMethod;
union isfuzzy=true DockerActivity, WebActivity
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Portainer plugin management API access (CVE-2026-44848) Exploitation High
Hunts HTTP POST requests to Portainer's /docker/plugins/pull and /docker/plugins/{name}/enable proxy endpoints, which bypass Portainer-side RBAC in vulnerable releases (<2.33.8, <2.39.2, <2.41.0) because /plugins is absent from prefixProxyFuncMap and falls through to executeDockerRequest unauthorized. Rationale: Article identifies the exact vulnerable endpoints (POST /plugins/pull, POST /plugins/{name}/enable) and shows in the Go source excerpt that /plugins is NOT in prefixProxyFuncMap so it bypasses Portainer's authorization wrapper. A successful POST against this URI from a non-admin session is unambiguous exploitation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4
ATT&CKT1190 T1068

[LLM] Docker plugin runtime spawned from /var/lib/docker/plugins/ on host (CVE-2026-44848) Installation High
Hunts Linux process executions whose binary path begins with /var/lib/docker/plugins/<digest>/rootfs/ and whose parent is dockerd/containerd/runc. Any post-exploit plugin pushed through the unauthorized /plugins/pull + /plugins/{name}/enable chain lands here and executes as root with whatever capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, host bind mounts) the plugin manifest requested. Rationale: Article states 'Docker plugins execute as root on the host' and the Linux runtime path for an enabled plugin is /var/lib/docker/plugins/<digest>/rootfs/. Pairing that image-path prefix with a containerd/dockerd parent yields a near-zero-FP signal because plugin install is normally an admin-only, low-frequency event. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4 • https://docs.docker.com/engine/extend/plugin_api/

[LLM] Docker daemon plugin install/enable event from non-admin context (CVE-2026-44848) Installation Medium
Surfaces dockerd syslog entries recording plugin pull/install/enable operations. Combined with UC1 (HTTP) and UC2 (process), this is the daemon-side proof of plugin registration and remains useful on hosts that do not run EDR but ship dockerd journald/syslog to the SIEM. Rationale: Article's affected-code excerpt shows requests fall through to executeDockerRequest and are forwarded to dockerd, so the dockerd log is the daemon-side fingerprint of /plugins/pull and /plugins/{name}/enable activity. This UC corroborates UC1+UC2 on hosts without EDR. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4

Hunt for hosts running n8n (Node.js parent process or n8n-nodes-base in cmdline) so SOC can cross-reference patched-version state against CVE-2026-44791. This is asset-surface enumeration for the n8n RCE patch bypass — runs read-only and identifies hosts to escalate to vulnerability management. Rationale: Article explicitly names affected packages npm:n8n with version ranges <1.123.43 / 2.20.7 / 2.22.1 and lists NODES_EXCLUDE=n8n-nodes-base.xml as the only workaround. [LLM] n8n Node.js parent spawning OS shell — post-exploit RCE indicator for CVE-2026-44791 Exploitation High
Detects the realised RCE outcome of the XML-node prototype-pollution patch bypass: an n8n Node.js process (commandline references n8n / n8n-nodes-base) spawning cmd/powershell/sh/bash with download, base64, reverse-shell, or temp-directory cmdline hallmarks. Article states 'when combined with other nodes, this could lead to RCE on the n8n host' — this catches that exact host-side execution shape. Rationale: Article: 'When combined with other nodes, this could lead to RCE on the n8n host.' n8n runs as a Node.js process; the prototype-pollution → RCE chain manifests as the Node parent spawning an OS shell with attacker-controlled cmdline. Parent fingerprint = node + n8n in cmdline (high-precision asset filter). Child = shell binary. Cmdline tokens = the standard reverse-shell / download cradle vocabulary from public n8n CVE-2026-44789/44790/44791 trio writeups (cross-checked against the CyberSecurityNews coverage that catalogs the trio). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories/GHSA-hqr4-h3xv-9m3r • https://cybersecuritynews.com/n8n-rce-vulnerabilities/

let Lookback = 7d;
let ShellChildren = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh"]);
let SusTokens = dynamic(["curl ","wget ","Invoke-WebRequest","IEX","Invoke-Expression","base64 ","-EncodedCommand","/tmp/","%TEMP%","bash -i","nc -e","perl -e","python -c"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has "\\node.exe"
  | extend ChildBin = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,"\\")[-1]))
  | where ChildBin in (ShellChildren)
  | where CommandLine has_any (SusTokens) or CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)/dev/tcp/"
  | where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = TargetUserName,
            ParentCmd = ParentProcessName, ChildImage = NewProcessName, ChildCmd = CommandLine),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
  | where ParentProcessName has "node"
  | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("n8n","n8n-nodes-base")
  | extend ChildBin = tolower(tostring(split(ActingProcessName,"/")[-1]))
  | where ChildBin in (ShellChildren)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (SusTokens) or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)/dev/tcp/"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername,
            ParentCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine, ChildImage = ActingProcessName, ChildCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44791")

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] n8n workflow API request body containing JS prototype pollution tokens (CVE-2026-44789) Exploitation High
Hunts for HTTP requests to the n8n workflow/execution API whose body or query string contains JavaScript prototype-pollution sentinels (`__proto__`, `constructor.prototype`, `__defineGetter__`) targeting the HTTP Request node pagination parameter. This is the article-specific pre-exploit signal for CVE-2026-44789. Rationale: Pivots on the exact prototype-pollution sentinels (`__proto__`, `constructor.prototype`, `__defineGetter__`) named in CWE-1321 / GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h, scoped to the n8n REST/webhook URL surface where the pagination parameter is parsed. Cross-checked against GitHub GHSA advisory, Endor Labs write-up, and Cybersecurity News reporting. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44789 • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/ • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1321.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007

| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemotePort in (5678, 443, 80) or LocalPort in (5678, 443, 80)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("node.exe", "n8n.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "n8n"
| where RemoteUrl has_any (PollutionTokens)
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (PollutionTokens)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, LocalPort, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,

| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;

    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientIP = cIP, User = csUserName,
              Method = csMethod, Uri = csUriStem, Query = csUriQuery, UA = csUserAgent,
              Source = "W3CIISLog";
let CSLHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RequestURL has_any ("/rest/workflows", "/rest/executions", "/webhook")

    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DestinationHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP,
              User = SourceUserName, Method = RequestMethod, Uri = RequestURL,

let WebHits = ImWebSession

description: Detects HTTP requests to n8n workflow/execution/webhook API endpoints whose URI or query string carries JavaScript prototype-pollution sentinel tokens used to exploit CVE-2026-44789 in the HTTP Request node pagination handler.
references:

[LLM] Post-exploit RCE: node.js (n8n) spawning shell or scripting interpreter Installation High
Detects the post-exploitation tail of CVE-2026-44789 — the n8n `node` process spawning a shell (`cmd.exe`, `sh`, `bash`, `powershell.exe`) or a LOLBin. Prototype-pollution RCEs land here because the polluted global lets the attacker reroute child-process spawning into arbitrary commands run as the n8n service account. Rationale: Uses the most reliable post-exploit signal — n8n's `node` process spawning a shell or LOLBin — which is the actual outcome chain described in GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h ("combined with other techniques this could lead to RCE"). Article + Endor Labs corroboration both flag RCE as the impact, and CWE-1321 prototype-pollution chains universally land via hijacked child-process spawn. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44789 • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1321.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1059 T1059.001 T1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes

let ShellsAndLolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","zsh","dash","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","nc","ncat","socat"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("n8n", "\\n8n\\", "/n8n/")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("n8n", "\\.n8n\\")
| where FileName in~ (ShellsAndLolbins)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ShellsAndLolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","zsh","dash","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","nc","ncat","socat"]);
let WinHits = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node\\","\\node")
    | where tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]) in~ (ShellsAndLolbins)
    | where (CommandLine has_any ("n8n")) or (ParentProcessName has "n8n") or true
    | where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, User=TargetUserName,
              ParentImage=ParentProcessName, ChildImage=NewProcessName,

let AsimHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")

[LLM] Vulnerable n8n versions in TVM inventory (CVE-2026-44789) Reconnaissance High
Surfaces hosts and software packages where n8n is installed at a version inside the CVE-2026-44789 vulnerable range (<1.123.43, 2.0.0-rc.0–2.20.6, 2.21.0–2.22.0). Pre-exploit asset visibility — without this UC the SOC is hunting blind for an attack surface they don't know they own. Rationale: Article explicitly enumerates vulnerable version ranges (npm:n8n <1.123.43; 2.0.0-rc.0–<2.20.7; 2.21.0–<2.22.1) — version-range matching against TVM inventory is the lowest-FP detection possible and the most operationally valuable pre-attack signal. Corroborated against the NVD CVE entry and the published patched versions. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c8xv-5998-g76h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44789
ATT&CKT1592.002 T1190
Data sources
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareName =~ "n8n" or SoftwareName has "n8n"
| extend Parts = split(SoftwareVersion, ".")
| extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Patch = toint(Parts[2])
| extend Vulnerable = case(
    Major == 1 and (Minor < 123 or (Minor == 123 and Patch < 43)), "yes-1.x (<1.123.43)",
    Major == 2 and Minor >= 0 and Minor <= 19, strcat("yes-2.", tostring(Minor), " (<2.20.7)"),
    Major == 2 and Minor == 20 and Patch < 7, "yes-2.20.<7",
    Major == 2 and Minor == 21, "yes-2.21 (<2.22.1)",
    Major == 2 and Minor == 22 and Patch < 1, "yes-2.22.0",
    "no")
| where Vulnerable != "no"
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId | project DeviceId, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, Vulnerable, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-44789" or SoftwareName has "n8n"
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId | project DeviceId, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform) on DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion,
          CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
(source:cspm OR source:tenable OR source:qualys OR source:rapid7) (@vulnerability.cve:CVE-2026-44789 OR (@software.name:n8n AND @software.version:(1.* OR 2.0.* OR 2.1.* OR 2.2.* OR 2.3.* OR 2.4.* OR 2.5.* OR 2.6.* OR 2.7.* OR 2.8.* OR 2.9.* OR 2.10.* OR 2.11.* OR 2.12.* OR 2.13.* OR 2.14.* OR 2.15.* OR 2.16.* OR 2.17.* OR 2.18.* OR 2.19.* OR 2.20.0 OR 2.20.1 OR 2.20.2 OR 2.20.3 OR 2.20.4 OR 2.20.5 OR 2.20.6 OR 2.21.* OR 2.22.0)))

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44789")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44789")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] Inbound exploit attempt to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager from known UAT-8616 / Cluster IPs Exploitation High
Detects network connections from the Talos-published exploit-source IPs targeting Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager / vSmart (vManage) management interfaces. Anchors on the specific source IPs Talos attributes to UAT-8616 and Clusters 1-4 exploiting CVE-2026-20182 and the CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122 chain. Rationale: Source IPs are explicitly attributed by Talos to UAT-8616 (CVE-2026-20182) and Clusters 1-4 (CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122). Ports cover vManage HTTPS (443/8443), NETCONF (830), SD-WAN device control (4566), and SSH (22). Cross-checked with Cisco PSIRT advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-auth-bypass and Rapid7's disclosure referenced in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/publicationListing.x • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/

[LLM] XenShell / Godzilla / Behinder JSP webshell file write on Cisco SD-WAN Manager Installation High
Detects creation of the specific JSP webshell filenames Talos observed dropped on compromised Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager nodes after exploitation of CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122. Filenames are non-generic and attacker-chosen (20251117022131.jsp, conf.jsp, sysv.jsp, sysinit.jsp, vmurnp_ikp.jsp). Rationale: Filenames 20251117022131.jsp, conf.jsp, sysv.jsp, sysinit.jsp, vmurnp_ikp.jsp are explicitly named by Talos as attacker-dropped XenShell/Godzilla/Behinder variants on the SD-WAN Manager. Generic .jsp creation under vManage webapps directories also catches XenShell variants with rotating names since SD-WAN Manager should not be receiving developer-dropped JSPs in production. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/ • https://github.com/BeichenDream/Godzilla

[LLM] AdaptixC2 'shadowcore' / Mythic C2 traffic to UAT-8616 infrastructure 194.163.175.135 Command & Control High
Detects outbound traffic to the AdaptixC2/Mythic infrastructure Talos attributes to UAT-8616 — IP 194.163.175.135 hosting AdaptixC2 on port 4445 (banner renamed from 'AdapticC2 server' to 'shadowcore'), another AdaptixC2 listener on 31337, and a Mythic C2 listener on 7443 with certificate serial fece5b954e69b2c6a8d0a1029631a0d7. Rationale: 194.163.175.135 plus the trio of ports (4445 AdaptixC2 with 'shadowcore' banner, 7443 Mythic, 31337 second AdaptixC2 listener) and the Mythic cert serial fece5b954e69b2c6a8d0a1029631a0d7 are explicitly published by Talos as UAT-8616 infrastructure on Contabo GmbH. The IP-and-port tuple is high-fidelity because legitimate enterprise traffic to a Contabo VPS on these obscure ports is exceedingly rare. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/sd-wan-ongoing-exploitation/ • https://github.com/Adaptix-Framework/AdaptixC2 • https://github.com/its-a-feature/Mythic

[LLM] AdaptixC2 'systemd-resolved' or Sliver 'CWan' implant on Linux / SD-WAN host Installation High
Detects the specific implant filenames Talos observed dropped post-exploitation on Cisco SD-WAN devices: 'systemd-resolved' (AdaptixC2 agent masquerading as the legitimate Linux service) calling 194.163.175.135:4445, and 'CWan' (Sliver implant) calling mtls://23.27.143.170:443. Hunts both the file presence and the C2 callouts. Rationale: Talos explicitly names the implant filenames ('systemd-resolved' for AdaptixC2 and 'CWan' for Sliver) and the C2 endpoints (194.163.175.135:4445, mtls://23.27.143.170:443). The masquerade check excludes the legitimate /lib/systemd path for systemd-resolved, so any other path equals a high-fidelity hit. Verified Sliver and AdaptixC2 framework attribution via the public AdaptixC2 and Sliver project pages. [LLM] UAT-8616 post-compromise on SD-WAN: SSH key add, NETCONF edit, su root, XMRig miner.sh Actions on Objectives High
Detects the specific post-compromise actions Talos lists for UAT-8616 after exploitation of CVE-2026-20182/20127 — adding SSH keys, modifying NETCONF configuration, privilege escalation via 'su root -c id', plus Cluster 7's XMRig deployment via /tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh with config_background.json. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article's verbatim strings: Code Block 2 (/tmp/moneroocean/miner.sh --config=/tmp/moneroocean/config_background.json), Code Block 3 (su root -c id), and the named post-compromise actions Talos lists for UAT-8616 (SSH key addition, NETCONF configuration modification). The 'su root -c id' command is a UAT-8616 fingerprint — a sophisticated actor verifying root context after privilege escalation, not normal admin usage. [LLM] FlowiseAI POST /api/v1/node-custom-function with NodeVM Sandbox-Escape Payload (CVE-2026-46442) Exploitation High
Hunts authenticated POST requests to the unprotected Flowise custom-function endpoint that carry the specific NodeVM-escape payload markers documented in CVE-2026-46442 (constructor.constructor, getBuiltinModule, child_process, execSync, error.name=Object.create). High fidelity because the URL is article-specific and the payload tokens are the exact escape primitive. Rationale: Three article-specific anchors: the exact endpoint path /api/v1/node-custom-function, the JSON body field name javascriptFunction, and the documented escape primitive (constructor.constructor / getBuiltinModule / child_process). The URL is unique to Flowise; the body markers are the exact NodeVM-escape technique cited in the GHSA. Cross-checked against the @flowiseai/nodevm fork and prior vm2 sandbox-escape literature (Semgrep, BleepingComputer). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9rvc-vf7m-pgm2 • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/nodevm • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/ • https://www.npmjs.com/package/@flowiseai/nodevm
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007 T1068
Data sourcesWeb
// IIS / App Service in front of Flowise (URL pivot — most reverse proxies don't log POST body)
let ProxyHits =
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriStem has "/api/v1/node-custom-function"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, cIP, csUserName, csUserAgent, scStatus, sPort;
// WAF / proxy that DOES log body or the request URL with payload markers
let WafHits =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
    | where RequestURL has "/api/v1/node-custom-function"
       or Message has_any ("constructor.constructor", "getBuiltinModule", "javascriptFunction", "child_process")
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, Message, DeviceAction;
union isfuzzy=true ProxyHits, WafHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Flowise node.exe Spawning OS Shell or Command-Line Utility - Post-Exploit RCE (CVE-2026-46442) Exploitation High
Detects the Flowise Node.js host process spawning a child shell or built-in OS utility (cmd, powershell, sh, bash, wmic, whoami, id, hostname, ipconfig) - the exact post-conditions of the documented NodeVM escape that calls child_process.execSync. The PoC literally runs 'id' as the validation payload. Rationale: The PoC in the advisory ends with cp.execSync('id') - guaranteeing node.exe forks a shell/utility. Parent=node.exe + parent-cmd contains flowise/packages/server + child=shell-or-recon is a combination that should never occur during normal Flowise operation; the application is a JS chatflow engine, not a process orchestrator. Pivot is high-fidelity because the parent context is article-specific. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9rvc-vf7m-pgm2 • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/nodevm • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/
ATT&CKT1059 T1059.003 T1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("flowise", "packages/server", "packages\\server", "@flowiseai")
     or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("flowise", "Flowise", "@flowiseai")
| where FileName in~ (
    "cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
    "wmic.exe","whoami.exe","hostname.exe","ipconfig.exe","net.exe",
    "net1.exe","netstat.exe","tasklist.exe","systeminfo.exe","reg.exe",
    "sh","bash","dash","zsh","id","uname","ifconfig","ip","ps",
    "curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat"
  )
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath,
          ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Windows 4688 view
let WinHits =
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName endswith "\\node.exe"
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("flowise", "Flowise", "@flowiseai", "packages\\server")
         or CommandLine has_any ("flowise", "Flowise")
    | where NewProcessName has_any (
        "\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe",
        "\\wmic.exe","\\whoami.exe","\\hostname.exe","\\ipconfig.exe","\\net.exe",
        "\\reg.exe","\\tasklist.exe","\\systeminfo.exe","\\curl.exe")
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
              ParentProcessName, SubjectUserName;
// Linux / ASIM view
let LinuxHits =
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ParentProcessName endswith "/node" or ParentProcessName == "node"
    | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("flowise", "packages/server", "@flowiseai")
    | where TargetProcessName endswith_cs "/sh"
         or TargetProcessName endswith_cs "/bash"
         or TargetProcessName endswith_cs "/dash"
         or TargetProcessName endswith_cs "/zsh"
         or TargetProcessName in ("id","uname","whoami","hostname","ifconfig","ip","ps","curl","wget","nc","ncat")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
              ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine;
union isfuzzy=true WinHits, LinuxHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Strapi CVE-2026-27886 exploit — `where[admin-relation][private-field]` query parameter against public Content API Exploitation High
Detects HTTP requests that abuse Strapi's relational filtering bug (CVE-2026-27886) by traversing `updatedBy`/`createdBy`/`publishedBy` joins into the `admin_users` table to read private fields such as `resetPasswordToken`, `email`, or `password`. The query parameter shape is unique to this vulnerability and rarely produced by legitimate clients. Rationale: Uses the exact malicious query-parameter regex published in the GHSA advisory (`where[updatedBy|createdBy|publishedBy][resetPasswordToken|password|email|...][$startsWith|...]=`). This shape is unique to the CVE-2026-27886 exploit chain — legitimate Strapi clients filter by content-type fields, never by admin-relation private fields. corroborated_sources field references the GHSA primary source. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rjg2-95x7-8qmx

[LLM] Strapi boolean-oracle hex-alphabet brute force from single source Exploitation High
Detects the high-volume single-source brute-force pattern characteristic of CVE-2026-27886 oracle extraction: the same Content API endpoint hit dozens-to-hundreds of times from one IP with identical-shape `where[adminRel][field][$op]=<hex>` query strings where only the trailing filter value varies across the hex alphabet (`0`–`f`). Threshold-and-cardinality detection. Rationale: The article's IoC list explicitly calls out: 'High volume of public Content API requests from a single IP iterating through a hex alphabet (0-9, a-f) on the same content-type endpoint with progressively-longer filter values' and 'Sustained burst of identical-shape requests with only the trailing character of the filter value varying'. The detection codifies that — high request count + ≥16 distinct hex filter values + tight time window — into a threshold trigger. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rjg2-95x7-8qmx
ATT&CKT1212 T1190 T1110.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 6h;
let MinRequestsPerSource = 50;
let MinDistinctFilterValues = 16;  // hex alphabet width: 0-9,a-f
let MaxDurationSec = 1800;          // burst must be tight (~30 min) to count as oracle
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)where\[(updatedBy|createdBy|publishedBy)\]\[(email|password|resetPasswordToken|confirmationToken|firstname|lastname|preferedLanguage)\]\[\$"
| extend FilterValue = extract(@"(?i)where\[\w+\]\[\w+\]\[\$\w+\]=([0-9a-fA-F]+)", 1, Url)
| extend FilterFieldTuple = extract(@"(?i)(where\[\w+\]\[\w+\]\[\$\w+\])=", 1, Url)
| where isnotempty(FilterValue)
| summarize
    RequestCount   = count(),
    DistinctValues = dcount(FilterValue),
    SampleValues   = make_set(FilterValue, 20),
    DistinctTuples = dcount(FilterFieldTuple),
    SampleTuples   = make_set(FilterFieldTuple, 5),
    UAs            = make_set(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, 5),
    FirstSeen      = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen       = max(TimeGenerated)
    by SrcIpAddr, HttpHostName
| extend DurationSec = datetime_diff('second', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| where RequestCount >= MinRequestsPerSource and DistinctValues >= MinDistinctFilterValues and DurationSec <= MaxDurationSec
| order by RequestCount desc

[LLM] Strapi CVE-2026-27886 admin takeover — exploit burst followed by `/admin/reset-password` POST Actions on Objectives High
Correlates a burst of CVE-2026-27886 oracle-extraction requests against a Strapi host with a subsequent `POST /admin/reset-password` call on the same host within 30 minutes. This is the closing move of the documented account-takeover chain: oracle-extract a reset token, then call the admin reset-password endpoint with it. Rationale: The article's IoC list specifies two final-stage signals: 'Subsequent POST /admin/reset-password calls using a reset token that the legitimate admin did not request' and 'Successful admin password change immediately following a burst of public Content API requests with where[updatedBy] query parameters'. The detection chains them at the per-host level with a 30-minute follow-on window — the same shape as the documented end-to-end takeover. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rjg2-95x7-8qmx
ATT&CKT1078 T1212 T1098
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let ChainWindow   = 30min;
let MinExploitReqs = 10;
let StrapiExploitRegex = @"(?i)where\[(updatedBy|createdBy|publishedBy)\]\[(email|password|resetPasswordToken|confirmationToken|firstname|lastname|preferedLanguage)\]\[\$";
let ExploitBursts =
    ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where Url matches regex StrapiExploitRegex
    | summarize ExploitCount = count(), FirstExploit = min(TimeGenerated), LastExploit = max(TimeGenerated), ExploitSrcIPs = make_set(SrcIpAddr, 10) by HttpHostName
    | where ExploitCount >= MinExploitReqs;
let ResetCalls =
    ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where Url has "/admin/reset-password"
    | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
    | project ResetTime = TimeGenerated, ResetHost = HttpHostName, ResetSrcIp = SrcIpAddr, ResetUrl = Url, ResetUA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent;
ExploitBursts
| join kind=inner ResetCalls on $left.HttpHostName == $right.ResetHost
| where ResetTime between (FirstExploit .. (LastExploit + ChainWindow))
| extend ChainLatencySec = datetime_diff('second', ResetTime, LastExploit)
| project FirstExploit, LastExploit, ResetTime, ChainLatencySec, HttpHostName, ExploitCount, ExploitSrcIPs, ResetSrcIp, ResetUrl, ResetUA
| order by ResetTime desc

[LLM] Vulnerable Amazon Redshift JDBC Driver (CVE-2026-8178) inventory hunt — redshift-jdbc42 < 2.2.2 Reconnaissance High
Surfaces every host/asset where Defender TVM (or equivalent vuln scanner) reports the Amazon Redshift JDBC Driver below the patched 2.2.2 release, so the SOC can prioritise patching/segmentation of the JVMs whose classpath could be weaponised through CVE-2026-8178. Rationale: Pivots on the explicit CVE id and the affected Maven coordinate (`com.amazon.redshift:redshift-jdbc42` < 2.2.2) called out in the GHSA. Since the article confirms the fix landed in 2.2.2, the version-prefix exclusion list (2.2.2/.3/.4/.5/.6) is a precise inventory filter — false positives only when TVM lags on a freshly patched host. Joining DeviceInfo flags Internet-facing JVM hosts so the SOC can sequence patching by exposure. Datadog left blank because TVM CVE coverage is not shipped to Datadog logs in this estate; Sigma left blank because TVM is a snapshot, not an event-shaped log. [LLM] CVE-2026-8178 exploit attempt: Redshift JDBC URL with class-loading parameter (socketFactory/sslfactory/sslhostnameverifier/sslpasswordcallb Exploitation High
Hunts for the specific exploit primitive of CVE-2026-8178 — a `jdbc:redshift://` connection string carrying one of the four parameters (`socketFactory`, `sslfactory`, `sslhostnameverifier`, `sslpasswordcallback`) the unpatched driver instantiates without type-checking. Surfaces the URL whether it appears in a JVM command line, a connection-string env-var passed at fork, or a webapp HTTP request that accepts user-supplied JDBC URLs (DataEase-style sink). Rationale: The four parameter names (`socketFactory`, `sslfactory`, `sslhostnameverifier`, `sslpasswordcallback`) are the documented type-confusion sinks where the unpatched driver `Class.forName()`-then-instantiates whatever class name the JDBC URL specifies — confirmed by the AWS security bulletin and the related historical advisory chain (CVE-2022-41828, CVE-2024-12744). Pairing them with the `jdbc:redshift` scheme literal and the `java.exe`/`javaw.exe` image gives a 3-of-3 high-fidelity composite that has effectively zero benign use. The web-tier branch catches the DataEase-style sink where a webapp accepts user-supplied JDBC URLs (corroborated by GHSA-mfg2-qr5c-99pp). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/aws/amazon-redshift-jdbc-driver/security/advisories/GHSA-wmmv-vvg5-993q • https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/rss/2026-028-aws/ • https://github.com/murataydemir/CVE-2022-41828 • https://github.com/dataease/dataease/security/advisories/GHSA-mfg2-qr5c-99pp • https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/AWS-2024-015/

let vuln_params = dynamic(["socketFactory=","sslfactory=","sslhostnameverifier=","sslpasswordcallback="]);
let jdbc_pivot  = dynamic(["jdbc:redshift","jdbc%3aredshift"]);
let ProcessHits =

union isfuzzy=true ProcessHits, WebHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Kimsuky HelloDoor 'tdll' Run-key persistence with regsvr32 loader Installation High
Hunts the autorun footprint of HelloDoor, Kimsuky's first Rust-based PebbleDash variant. HelloDoor uniquely registers itself under HKCU\...\Run with the value name 'tdll' and a data string invoking 'regsvr32.exe /s [DLL path]'. The combination of that exact value name and a regsvr32 silent-load command in a Run key is article-specific and not seen in benign software. Rationale: The article explicitly names the Run-key value 'tdll' and data 'regsvr32.exe /s [current file path]' as HelloDoor's persistence routine. 'tdll' has no documented benign use and the regsvr32 silent flag adds further specificity. Token-aligned matches on the registry path and value data make this a tight, low-FP detection. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/kimsuky-appleseed-pebbledash-campaigns/119785/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1218.010
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "tdll"
| where RegistryValueData has "regsvr32" and RegistryValueData has "/s"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValue =~ "tdll"
| where RegistryValueData has "regsvr32" and RegistryValueData has "/s"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Kimsuky httpMalice persistence: 'Everything 1.9a-/1.8a-' Run-key or CacheDB service install Installation High
Hunts httpMalice (latest PebbleDash backdoor variant) establishing persistence. Depending on token elevation, it either creates a service named 'CacheDB' (display name 'Administrator', running 'rundll32.exe [dll path], load') or writes an HKCU Run-key value named 'Everything 1.9a-[filesize]' (or older 'Everything 1.8a-[filesize]'). Both indicators are uniquely tied to httpMalice. Rationale: The article literally names 'Everything 1.9a-[filesize]' / 'Everything 1.8a-[filesize]' as the Run-key value names httpMalice writes, and 'CacheDB' (with 'rundll32.exe [DLL], load' image path and 'Administrator' display name) as the service it creates when elevated. Both strings are bespoke to httpMalice — joining registry + service-install telemetry captures both code paths. Sigma omitted because the rule is a union of two distinct event shapes (registry value set + service install). Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/kimsuky-appleseed-pebbledash-campaigns/119785/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1543.003 T1218.011
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Services
union
(DeviceRegistryEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
  | where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"
  | where RegistryValueName matches regex @"(?i)^Everything 1\.[89]a-\d+$"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            Signal = "httpMalice RunKey (Everything 1.9a-/1.8a-)",
            Detail = strcat(RegistryValueName, " => ", RegistryValueData)),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType == "ServiceInstalled"
  | extend AF = parse_json(AdditionalFields)
  | extend SvcName = tostring(AF.ServiceName), SvcImage = tostring(AF.ServiceFileName)
  | where SvcName =~ "CacheDB"
  | where SvcImage has "rundll32" and SvcImage has ",load"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            Signal = "httpMalice CacheDB service install",
            Detail = SvcImage)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(ImRegistryEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"
  | where RegistryValue matches regex @"(?i)^Everything 1\.[89]a-\d+$"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
            Signal = "httpMalice RunKey (Everything 1.9a-/1.8a-)",
            Detail = strcat(RegistryValue, " => ", RegistryValueData)),
(Event
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventLog == "System" and EventID == 7045
  | where RenderedDescription has "CacheDB"
  | where RenderedDescription has "rundll32" and RenderedDescription has ",load"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = Computer, ActorUsername = UserName, ActingProcessName = "services.exe",
            Signal = "httpMalice CacheDB service install",
            Detail = RenderedDescription)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
