[LLM] Kimsuky JSE dropper: wscript -> powershell hidden + certutil -decode chain Delivery High
Hunts the literal command-line emitted by Kimsuky's JSE droppers (HelloDoor, httpMalice, AppleSeed deliveries): 'powershell.exe -windowstyle hidden certutil -decode [src] [dst]'. The dropper executes via wscript.exe (default JSE handler), shells PowerShell hidden, and uses certutil to base64-decode the second-stage payload before invoking it with regsvr32/rundll32. Rationale: Direct quote from the article: 'The malicious payload leverages powershell.exe -windowstyle hidden certutil -decode [src path] [dst path] for the second Base64 decoding before execution.' JSE files are handled by wscript.exe by default. The four-token combination (windowstyle + hidden + certutil + -decode in one cmdline, parented by a script host) is essentially never seen in benign software. Defender query also chains to the follow-on regsvr32/rundll32 from C:\ProgramData mentioned in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/kimsuky-appleseed-pebbledash-campaigns/119785/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/ • https://lolbas-project.github.io/lolbas/Binaries/Certutil/
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.005 T1140 T1564.003 T1218.010
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "powershell.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "windowstyle" and ProcessCommandLine has "hidden"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "certutil" and ProcessCommandLine has "-decode"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","explorer.exe","cmd.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("regsvr32.exe","rundll32.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "powershell.exe"
    | where FolderPath has @"C:\ProgramData" or ProcessCommandLine has @"C:\ProgramData"
    | project FollowOnTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, FollowOnCmd = ProcessCommandLine, FollowOnFile = FileName
  ) on DeviceName
| where isnull(FollowOnTime) or FollowOnTime between (Timestamp .. Timestamp + 5m)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName endswith "powershell.exe"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "windowstyle" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "hidden"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "certutil" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "-decode"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","explorer.exe","cmd.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7") or SHA1 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7") or MD5 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7") or SHA1 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7") or MD5 in~ ("995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — Kimsuky targets organizations with PebbleDash-based tools Exploitation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027 T1053.005 T1053.005 T1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Kimsuky targets organizations with PebbleDash-based tools
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ (".hwp.jse", "hwpx.jse", ".hwpx.jse", "security_20260126.scr", "pdf.jse", "hyun-jung.pdf.jse", "memloader.dll", "unrar.exe", "dwagsvc.exe", "secu.scr", "xipbkmaw.exe") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-WindowStyle Hidden") or FolderPath has_any ("C:\programdata\unrar.exe", "C:\programdata\1.zip"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("C:\programdata\unrar.exe", "C:\programdata\1.zip") or FileName in~ (".hwp.jse", "hwpx.jse", ".hwpx.jse", "security_20260126.scr", "pdf.jse", "hyun-jung.pdf.jse", "memloader.dll", "unrar.exe", "dwagsvc.exe", "secu.scr", "xipbkmaw.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

[LLM] FrostyNeighbor PicassoLoader drop to %AppData%\WinDataScope\Update.js Installation High
Hunts the article-specific second-stage drop: a JavaScript PicassoLoader payload written to a fixed AppData subfolder ('WinDataScope') used by FrostyNeighbor's March 2026 Ukrtelecom-themed compromise chain. The folder name and filename are both fingerprinted by ESET against multiple samples in this campaign. Rationale: WinDataScope is a folder name nowhere referenced in legitimate software inventories — ESET fingerprints it directly to FrostyNeighbor's PicassoLoader staging in the May 2026 report. Combined with the file name Update.js this is a near-zero-FP file-write signature. Cross-checked against: • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240 • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1010/ • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/
ATT&CKT1027.009 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has @"\AppData\Roaming\WinDataScope" and FileName =~ "Update.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA1, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated" or EventType =~ "FileModified"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\AppData\Roaming\WinDataScope" and TargetFileName =~ "Update.js"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath,
          TargetFileSHA1, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] FrostyNeighbor JS dropper self-relaunch with --update flag Exploitation High
Detects the FrostyNeighbor first-stage JavaScript dropper's documented self-relaunch pattern: wscript.exe / cscript.exe executes a .js file with the literal '--update' argument so the second branch of the script can install PicassoLoader. The flag string is bespoke to this campaign and is not used by legitimate Windows Script Host workflows. Rationale: The article explicitly states the first-stage script re-executes itself with the --update flag to branch into the PicassoLoader drop. The double-dash --update form is uncommon in WSH-launched JavaScript and pairs with a .js argument that is rarely seen in benign workflows. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/007/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--update"
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--update" and ActingProcessCommandLine has ".js"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] FrostyNeighbor C2 callout to needbinding/nebao/algsat/sardk/alexavegas/lavanille Command & Control High
Detects DNS or HTTP egress to the six FrostyNeighbor C2 domains published by ESET in May 2026 (PicassoLoader on five .icu hosts plus a .buzz Cobalt Strike host). All six share the same actor infrastructure cluster registered between 2026-03-10 and 2026-04-14. Rationale: ESET published the full domain list in Table 2 of the article alongside first-seen dates from a freshly-registered actor infrastructure cluster (.icu/.buzz, no legitimate corporate use). Any host in a UA/PL/LT/EE government estate touching these domains is high-fidelity actor traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1010/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let FrostyDomains = dynamic(["needbinding.icu","nebao.icu","algsat.icu","alexavegas.icu","sardk.icu","lavanille.buzz"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (FrostyDomains)
    | extend Source="NetworkEvent"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source;
let EventHits = DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where ActionType =~ "DnsQueryResponse"
    | extend QueriedDomain = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).DnsQueryString)
    | where QueriedDomain has_any (FrostyDomains)
    | extend Source="DnsQuery"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP="", RemoteUrl=QueriedDomain,
              RemotePort=tolong(0),
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, Source;
union NetHits, EventHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let FrostyDomains = dynamic(["needbinding.icu","nebao.icu","algsat.icu","alexavegas.icu","sardk.icu","lavanille.buzz"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where DnsQuery has_any (FrostyDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Domain=DnsQuery, Source="DNS"),
    (ImWebSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where Url has_any (FrostyDomains) or HttpHostName has_any (FrostyDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Domain=coalesce(HttpHostName,Url), Source="HTTP"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where RequestURL has_any (FrostyDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (FrostyDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr=SourceIP, SrcUsername=SourceUserName, Domain=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Source="FW")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PicassoLoader scheduled-task creation by wscript/cscript after C2 XML fetch Installation Medium
Detects FrostyNeighbor's persistence step: the JavaScript dropper downloads a scheduled-task XML template (served via the misleading Content-Type/Content-Disposition response to a .jpg URL) and then registers it. The parent-child chain of WSH spawning schtasks.exe or powershell.exe Register-ScheduledTask is article-specific. Rationale: The article describes the script downloading 'https://book-happy.needbinding[.]icu/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/1GreenAM.jpg' (which actually returns config.xml with Content-Type: application/xml) and then using it for persistence. Wscript/cscript spawning schtasks /Create /XML is a tight, low-FP pivot specific to this WSH-driven persistence pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where (FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Create","/XML"))
      or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Register-ScheduledTask")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ChildProcess=FileName, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcess=InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandparentProcess=InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where (ActingProcessName has "schtasks.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Create","/XML"))
      or (ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ActingProcessCommandLine has "Register-ScheduledTask")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: WSH-Initiated Scheduled Task Registration (FrostyNeighbor PicassoLoader)
id: 2c8f47a3-9b14-4ee5-b87e-91a4f5d63c11
description: Detects wscript.exe or cscript.exe spawning schtasks.exe /Create /XML or powershell Register-ScheduledTask. This is the persistence step in FrostyNeighbor's March 2026 PicassoLoader chain, in which an XML template is downloaded under a fake .jpg URL and registered as a scheduled task.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/frostyneighbor-fresh-mischief-digital-shenanigans/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/19
tags:
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  child_schtasks:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/Create'
      - '/XML'
  child_pwsh:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'Register-ScheduledTask'
  condition: parent and (child_schtasks or child_pwsh)
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate vendor installers that use JScript wrappers to register tasks (rare)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe OR *\\WSCRIPT.EXE OR *\\CSCRIPT.EXE)) ((@Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SchTasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*/Create* OR */XML*)) OR (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe) AND @CommandLine:*Register-ScheduledTask*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| (ImageFileName=/schtasks\.exe$/i AND regex("(/Create|/XML)", field=CommandLine))
  OR (ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND regex("Register-ScheduledTask", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

[LLM] FrostyNeighbor Cobalt Strike beacon ViberPC.dll image load Installation High
Detects loading of ViberPC.dll, the final-stage Cobalt Strike beacon FrostyNeighbor masquerades as the legitimate Viber desktop messenger DLL. ESET publishes a SHA-1 (43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB) and the file is expected outside the legitimate Viber install path under the standard Cobalt Strike beacon naming pattern Win32/CobaltStrike.Beacon.S. Rationale: ESET published the exact SHA-1 (43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB) for the ViberPC.dll Cobalt Strike beacon in Table 1, classified Win32/CobaltStrike.Beacon.S. Combined with masquerading detection — ViberPC.dll loaded from a non-Viber path — this is a high-confidence final-stage beacon detection. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1010/ • https://cert.gov.ua/article/40240
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1055.001 T1588.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let FrostyHashes = dynamic(["43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB"]);
let ImageLoads = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where FileName =~ "ViberPC.dll"
    | where SHA1 in~ (FrostyHashes)
         or not (FolderPath has @"\Viber\" or FolderPath has @"\Program Files\Viber")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="ImageLoad";
let FileWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where FileName =~ "ViberPC.dll"
    | where SHA1 in~ (FrostyHashes)
         or not (FolderPath has @"\Viber\" or FolderPath has @"\Program Files\Viber")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="FileWrite";
union ImageLoads, FileWrites
| order by Timestamp desc
let FrostyHashes = dynamic(["43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "ViberPC.dll"
| where TargetFileSHA1 in~ (FrostyHashes)
     or not (TargetFilePath has @"\Viber\" or TargetFilePath has @"\Program Files\Viber")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath,
          TargetFileSHA1, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects the ViberPC.dll Cobalt Strike beacon used by FrostyNeighbor (Ghostwriter/UNC1151) in May 2026, identified by ESET via SHA-1 43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB. Hash match OR ViberPC.dll loaded from a path outside the legitimate Viber install directory.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or SHA1 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or MD5 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or SHA1 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB") or MD5 in~ ("776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["776A43E46C36A539C916ED426745EE96E2392B39", "8D1F2A6DF51C7783F2EAF1A0FC0FF8D032E5B57F", "B65551D339AECE718EA1465BF3542C794C445EFC", "43E30BE82D82B24A6496F6943ECB6877E83F88AB"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Strapi Content-Type Builder Write API Reached in Production (CVE-2026-22599) Exploitation Medium
Detects POST/PUT to Strapi's Content-Type Builder write endpoint from a non-internal source. Per the patch (v5.33.2 / v4.26.1) these endpoints are disabled outside dev mode and return 404 — any successful POST/PUT in production indicates an unpatched instance under active exploitation or pre-patch admin misuse, both worth alerting on. Rationale: Anchored to the article's primary IOC — the literal endpoint path `/content-type-builder/content-types` and the (POST|PUT) verb regex. The patch behavior (404 in production) is what makes any such request high-signal: the article explicitly states the patch 'returns 404 for requests against /content-type-builder/content-types... removing the network-reachable attack surface entirely'. Splunk filters out RFC1918/loopback to focus on internet-reachable instances; Sentinel uses ImWebSession + not(ipv4_is_private) for the same effect. Defender Advanced Hunting has no native web access-log table, so defender_kql is empty (this telemetry lives in W3CIISLog / WAF logs, not DeviceProcessEvents).
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb
// Strapi Content-Type Builder endpoint should return 404 in production (v5.33.2+/v4.26.1+)
// Any POST/PUT reaching it from a non-internal source = exploit attempt or unpatched instance
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where HttpMethod in ("POST","PUT")
| where Url contains "/content-type-builder/content-types"
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr)
| where not(ipv4_is_private(SrcIpAddr))
| where not(SrcIpAddr startswith "127.")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpRequestHeaderReferer
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Strapi Content-Type Builder Write Followed by Server-Side Error (CVE-2026-22599 DoS / migration crash) Exploitation Medium
Detects POST/PUT to the Strapi Content-Type Builder content-types endpoint that returns a 5xx status — the article's explicit IOC for exploitation is 'Strapi server crashes immediately following a content-type creation or update, observed as the Node process exiting during the schema-migration step'. A 502/503/504 (upstream Strapi unreachable) or 500 from the Strapi node itself, gated to this specific URI, is a high-fidelity DoS / migration-error signal for the isRaw raw() injection. Rationale: Uses the article's explicit behavioural IOC — 'Strapi server crashes immediately following a content-type creation or update, observed as the Node process exiting during the schema-migration step'. A failed migration manifests as a 5xx on the same HTTP transaction (500 from Strapi itself, 502/503/504 from the upstream reverse proxy after node exits), so a single-event filter on (POST|PUT) + /content-type-builder/ + status≥500 is high-fidelity and Sigma-compatible. Datadog query left empty because the standard log sources listed (cloudtrail, azure.*, windows.*, linux.*, gcp.audit, kubernetes.audit, okta) do not include a generic web-access source — this telemetry would arrive at Datadog via a custom nginx/apache source not enumerated in the schema reference. Defender has no native web-access-log table.
ATT&CKT1190 T1499.004
Data sourcesWeb
// Schema-migration crash signature for CVE-2026-22599: 5xx response to a Content-Type Builder write
// Mirrors article IOC: 'Node process exiting during the schema-migration step'
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where HttpMethod in ("POST","PUT")
| where Url contains "/content-type-builder/"
| where HttpStatusCode between (500 .. 599)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), DistinctUrls = make_set(Url, 25), Statuses = make_set(HttpStatusCode, 10) by SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] SiYuan Electron renderer spawns shell/scripting child (CVE-2026-45375 Bazaar XSS → RCE) Exploitation High
Hunts the post-exploit RCE step of CVE-2026-45375. The SiYuan Bazaar XSS pivots to OS command execution via Node's child_process from a renderer with nodeIntegration=true. A SiYuan main/renderer process spawning cmd/powershell/pwsh/wscript/cscript/bash/sh/osascript/open/calc is highly anomalous — SiYuan is a markdown notes app and does not legitimately invoke shells. Rationale: Direct from the article: the renderer runs with `nodeIntegration:true`, `contextIsolation:false`, `webSecurity:false` (app/electron/main.js:407-411) and the Electron RCE PoC explicitly substitutes `require('child_process').exec('open -a Calculator')` as the payload string. Any shell/scripting child of siyuan.exe is therefore the executed payload. Cross-checked against memory observation 392 (SiYuan Electron RCE CVE cluster). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-27qc-m5gf-jv5r
ATT&CKT1059 T1203 T1189

[LLM] SiYuan Bazaar manifest written with embedded HTML/script markers (CVE-2026-45375 dropper) Delivery Medium
Hunts the dropper stage of CVE-2026-45375. A malicious Bazaar package's `plugin.json` / `theme.json` / `template.json` / `widget.json` / `icon.json` carrying HTML in the unsanitized `name` or `version` fields lands in the SiYuan workspace under `data/plugins/`, `data/themes/`, etc. Honest assumption: the file is dropped by something other than siyuan.exe itself (file-system sync, archive extraction, sideload) — siyuan.exe → manifest is the legitimate marketplace path. Targets the workspace manifest pattern named by the advisory. Rationale: Article names the exact five manifest filenames (plugin.json/theme.json/template.json/widget.json/icon.json), the exact workspace layout (`/tmp/siyuan-poc-ws/data/plugins/evil-plugin/plugin.json` in the Docker PoC), and the unescaped fields (`name`, `version`). FileSize > 2048 is a heuristic — clean manifests in the wild are ~200-600 bytes; the PoC payload bloats them. Tier=hunting because content inspection would be required to confirm the HTML payload — without it some baseline noise from legitimate marketplace installs is expected. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-27qc-m5gf-jv5r
ATT&CKT1546 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// CVE-2026-45375 — SiYuan Bazaar manifest dropped in workspace (potential payload carrier)
let _manifest_names = dynamic(["plugin.json","theme.json","template.json","widget.json","icon.json"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName in~ (_manifest_names)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\data\plugins\", @"\data\themes\", @"\data\templates\", @"\data\widgets\", @"\data\icons\",
                            "/data/plugins/", "/data/themes/", "/data/templates/", "/data/widgets/", "/data/icons/")
// honest manifests are tiny (~200-500 bytes); HTML/JS payload bloats them, OR a non-siyuan writer = sideload
| where FileSize > 2048
   or not(InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("siyuan.exe","siyuan"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45375 — Sentinel ASIM port
let _manifest_names = dynamic(["plugin.json","theme.json","template.json","widget.json","icon.json"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName in~ (_manifest_names)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\data\plugins\", @"\data\themes\", @"\data\templates\", @"\data\widgets\", @"\data\icons\",

| where TargetFileSize > 2048
   or not(ActingProcessName has_any ("siyuan.exe","siyuan"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath,

[LLM] Goobi viewer unauthenticated Solr streaming-expression proxy access (CVE-2026-45083) Exploitation High
Detects any HTTP request hitting the vulnerable Goobi viewer `/api/v[12]/index/stream` REST endpoint. The endpoint was removed in fix commit 326980f24c — on patched hosts this path should never appear in access logs; on unpatched hosts it should never be reachable from the public internet per the vendor's Apache/Tomcat block-list workaround. Any hit is therefore either a missed-patch indicator or active exploitation. Rationale: Endpoint path `/api/v[12]/index/stream` is the exact regex from the advisory's Apache httpd workaround block — no false-positive surface outside Goobi viewer. The fix removes the endpoint entirely, so any 2xx/3xx response is detection-grade. CIM Web datamodel + W3CIISLog + Sigma `webserver` category give cross-stack coverage; Defender XDR has no native HTTP request-path schema and is therefore omitted. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2rgp-f66f-4499 • https://solr.apache.org/guide/solr/latest/query-guide/streaming-expressions.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1212
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Goobi viewer CVE-2026-45083 — any access to the removed Solr streaming proxy
let GoobiEndpointRegex = @"(?i)/api/v[12]/index/stream";
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem matches regex GoobiEndpointRegex
| where csMethod in~ ("POST","GET")
| where scStatus !startswith "4" and scStatus !startswith "5"   // exclude denied/error
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName,
          csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus, TimeTaken
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Destructive Solr streaming expression (update/delete/commit) via Goobi viewer proxy Actions on Objectives High
Higher-fidelity follow-on to the endpoint-access detection — surfaces requests whose query string or body carries a destructive Solr streaming-expression function (`delete(`, `update(`, `commit(`). The advisory explicitly calls these out as enabling permanent index modification or full-collection deletion. Reads (`search(`) are intentionally excluded to keep the signal tight to integrity-impact exploitation. Rationale: Solr streaming expressions documented at solr.apache.org name `delete()`, `update()`, `commit()` as the integrity-impacting functions; the advisory explicitly cites `update()` and `delete()` as enabling field overwrite and full-collection deletion. Combining the article's exact endpoint regex with these function names yields near-zero FP surface — there is no legitimate caller of this endpoint after the patch (it was removed). URL-encoded `%28` variants are included to defeat trivial obfuscation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2rgp-f66f-4499 • https://solr.apache.org/guide/solr/latest/query-guide/streaming-expressions.html
ATT&CKT1485 T1565.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web

let GoobiEndpointRegex = @"(?i)/api/v[12]/index/stream";
let DestructiveFunctions = dynamic(["delete(", "update(", "commit("]);
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem matches regex GoobiEndpointRegex
| where csUriQuery has_any (DestructiveFunctions)
   or csUriQuery has "delete%28" or csUriQuery has "update%28" or csUriQuery has "commit%28"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName,
          csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus, TimeTaken
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives. [LLM] Obot /mcp-connect/{id} authenticated-user fan-out (ACR bypass probing) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp exploit pattern: a single authenticated Obot user hits 5+ distinct MCP server IDs via POST /mcp-connect/{id} inside 10 minutes. Legitimate users interact with 1-2 MCP servers; rapid enumeration across many IDs is the post-bypass discovery shape called out in the advisory's reproduction steps. Rationale: Built around the exact exploit primitive in the advisory's reproduction section — POST /mcp-connect/<mcp_server_id> with an authenticated session. Fan-out threshold (5 distinct IDs / 10m) reflects the attacker workflow of probing which IDs are reachable post-bypass; benign users discover MCP servers via the (correctly-gated) connector picker and stick to 1-2. Cross-checked GitHub advisory GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp; no public second-source PoCs surfaced. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp
ATT&CKT1190 T1078 T1213
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Obot ACR bypass — same user POSTing /mcp-connect/<id> against many distinct MCP server IDs in 10m
// Requires reverse proxy fronting Obot to be IIS-logging to Sentinel (W3CIISLog). For nginx/ALB/traefik
// use CommonSecurityLog / Syslog with the same regex on the URL path.
let WindowMin = 10m;
let FanoutThreshold = 5;     // empirical — legit users interact with 1-2 MCP servers
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where csMethod =~ "POST"
| where scStatus == 200
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)^/mcp-connect/[^/]+/?$"
| extend McpServerId = extract(@"(?i)^/mcp-connect/([^/?]+)", 1, csUriStem)
| where isnotempty(McpServerId)
| where isnotempty(csUserName)                 // authenticated only — anonymous would be 401
| summarize DistinctMcpIds = dcount(McpServerId),
            McpIdSet      = make_set(McpServerId, 50),
            HitCount      = count(),
            FirstSeen     = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen      = max(TimeGenerated),
            SrcIPs        = make_set(cIP, 10),
            UA            = any(csUserAgent)
            by csUserName, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where DistinctMcpIds >= FanoutThreshold
| project TimeGenerated, csUserName, DistinctMcpIds, McpIdSet, HitCount, FirstSeen, LastSeen, SrcIPs, UA
| order by DistinctMcpIds desc, LastSeen desc
source:nginx @http.method:POST @http.status_code:200 @http.url_details.path:*/mcp-connect/*
WEB

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rex field=SampledUrls "/mcp-connect/(?<McpId>[^/?\s\"]+)"

[LLM] First-time-seen authenticated user → MCP server ID pairing on /mcp-connect Actions on Objectives Medium
Anti-baseline hunt for GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp: surface a successful POST to /mcp-connect/<id> where the (user, mcp_server_id) pair has never been observed in the prior 30 days. Direct expression of the advisory's threat model — Basic Users reaching MCP servers they were never a member of any granting registry for. Rationale: Anti-baseline expression of the advisory's exact harm: a Basic User reaching an MCP server they were never a member of any granting MCP Registry for. The (csUserName, McpServerId) leftanti join surfaces novel pairings — the inverse of the legitimate intended flow described in the advisory's 'Vulnerability Details' section. Cross-checked against GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp; affected version <= v0.21.0. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vw82-7fv8-r6gp
ATT&CKT1078 T1213
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// First-time-seen Obot user → MCP server ID pair (anti-baseline against 30 days)
// Use this as a hunt; promote to alerting once baseline maturity is confirmed (>= 21 days of W3CIISLog retention).
let Lookback   = 30d;
let RecentWin  = 4h;
let ExtractMcpId = (s:string) { extract(@"(?i)^/mcp-connect/([^/?]+)", 1, s) };
let Baseline =
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(RecentWin))
    | where csMethod =~ "POST" and scStatus == 200
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)^/mcp-connect/[^/]+/?$"
    | extend McpServerId = ExtractMcpId(csUriStem)
    | where isnotempty(csUserName) and isnotempty(McpServerId)
    | summarize by csUserName, McpServerId;
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(RecentWin)
| where csMethod =~ "POST" and scStatus == 200
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)^/mcp-connect/[^/]+/?$"
| extend McpServerId = ExtractMcpId(csUriStem)
| where isnotempty(csUserName) and isnotempty(McpServerId)
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on csUserName, McpServerId
| summarize FirstHit  = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastHit   = max(TimeGenerated),
            HitCount  = count(),
            SrcIPs    = make_set(cIP, 10),
            UA        = any(csUserAgent)
            by csUserName, McpServerId
| order by FirstHit desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:

    category: file_access

detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'

    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser

level: high

[LLM] Mapfish Print Servlet running on host — CVE-2026-44672 exposure hunt Reconnaissance High
Identifies hosts where a Java process is running the Mapfish Print servlet (org.mapfish.print:print-lib / print-servlet) by anchoring on the Maven coordinates in the JVM command line. Use the output to enumerate exposure to CVE-2026-44672 (unauthenticated RCE in the Dynamic table feature) and reconcile installed version against patched matrix: >=3.23.0<3.28.28, >=3.29.0<3.30.30, >=3.31.0<3.31.21, >=3.32.0<3.33.14, >=3.34.0<4.0.3. Rationale: Article gives Maven coordinates org.mapfish.print:print-lib and org.mapfish.print:print-servlet plus the precise vulnerable version matrix. Anchoring on those strings inside java cmdline is high-fidelity (no other product uses these coords) and the regex extracts the running version so analysts can reconcile against the patched matrix in one pass. Cross-checked against the GHSA itself plus the Mapfish Print servlet source (MapPrinterServlet.java) and Jasper template injection background. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q7m6-wpvf-mvwx • https://github.com/mapfish/mapfish-print/blob/master/core/src/main/java/org/mapfish/print/servlet/MapPrinterServlet.java • https://insinuator.net/2023/06/jasper-reports-library-code-injection/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","java")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("mapfish-print","print-servlet","org.mapfish.print")
| extend MapfishVersion = extract(@"(?:print-lib|print-servlet|mapfish-print)-(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| extend Cve = "CVE-2026-44672",
         Note = "Vulnerable if 3.23.0-3.28.27, 3.29.0-3.30.29, 3.31.0-3.31.20, 3.32.0-3.33.13, 3.34.0-4.0.2"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine), Versions = make_set(MapfishVersion, 10)
            by DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, Cve, Note
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("java.exe","javaw.exe","java")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("mapfish-print","print-servlet","org.mapfish.print")
| extend MapfishVersion = extract(@"(?:print-lib|print-servlet|mapfish-print)-(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, TargetProcessCommandLine)

[LLM] OS shell or LOLBin spawned by Java process hosting Mapfish Print (CVE-2026-44672 exploit) Exploitation High
Hunts for command shells, scripting hosts, or recon LOLBins spawned as children of a java/javaw process whose own command line references the Mapfish Print servlet. Successful exploitation of CVE-2026-44672 (Jasper template injection in the Dynamic table feature) materialises as the JVM invoking Runtime.exec on attacker-supplied commands — visible here as java→cmd/powershell/bash/curl/whoami/etc. Rationale: The article specifies the exact Maven artifact (org.mapfish.print:print-lib / print-servlet) but no exploit-payload strings. The high-fidelity signal therefore comes from pairing (a) parent-process anchor = java/javaw whose cmdline contains the Mapfish Print coordinates with (b) child-process anchor = OS shells/LOLBins. java spawning a shell is anomalous for a Spring/Tomcat-hosted Mapfish Print process under normal operation and is the canonical post-exploitation footprint of Jasper template injection (Runtime.getRuntime().exec). Cross-checked against the Mapfish Print upstream servlet code and the Insinuator write-up on Jasper Reports template injection (same vuln class). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q7m6-wpvf-mvwx • https://github.com/mapfish/mapfish-print/blob/master/core/src/main/java/org/mapfish/print/servlet/MapPrinterServlet.java • https://insinuator.net/2023/06/jasper-reports-library-code-injection/

[LLM] SillyTavern CVE-2026-44650 unauthenticated POST to vulnerable /api/extensions/* endpoints Exploitation High
Detects POST requests to the five SillyTavern endpoints vulnerable to path-traversal-via-dot ('.') wipe of the user extensions directory: /api/extensions/{delete,update,version,branches,switch}. Targets the network/web-log pivot — the exploit is a single POST that returns HTTP 200 with a body referencing 'data\default-user\extensions'. Because no auth is required in default config (basicAuthMode:false), any source IP reaching the listener is suspect. Rationale: Article-specific URI stems are verbatim from the GHSA PoC (`POST /api/extensions/delete` with body `{"extensionName":"."}`) and the explicit 'Same Pattern in Other Endpoints' list (`/update`, `/version`, `/branches`, `/switch`). No auth means a single 200-OK POST to any of these paths is exploitation. Cross-checked against the DailyCVE write-up which confirms the same five endpoints and PoC shape. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-886q-f44j-h6wh • https://dailycve.com/sillytavern-unauthenticated-path-traversal-directory-deletion-cve-n-a-critical/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pkg/npm/sillytavern/CVE-2026-34524/
ATT&CKT1190 T1485
Data sourcesWeb
// Defender XDR has no native HTTP-server access-log table; this falls back to the egress pivot: a host that *initiated* a POST to a SillyTavern listener.
// Most useful where Defender-managed clients (browsers / curl from compromised hosts) hit the vulnerable instance.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/extensions/delete","/api/extensions/update","/api/extensions/version","/api/extensions/branches","/api/extensions/switch")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","python.exe","node.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
// Covers IIS-fronted, App-Service-fronted, CEF/firewall, and any ASIM-normalised web telemetry feeding the SillyTavern listener.
let vulnPaths = dynamic(["/api/extensions/delete","/api/extensions/update","/api/extensions/version","/api/extensions/branches","/api/extensions/switch"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod =~ "POST"
  | where csUriStem has_any (vulnPaths)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=cIP, DstHost=Computer, Method=csMethod, Uri=csUriStem, Status=scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent, Source="W3CIISLog"),
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where CsMethod =~ "POST"
  | where CsUriStem has_any (vulnPaths)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=CIp, DstHost=CsHost, Method=CsMethod, Uri=CsUriStem, Status=ScStatus, UserAgent=UserAgent, Source="AppServiceHTTPLogs"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
  | where RequestURL has_any (vulnPaths)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SourceIP, DstHost=DestinationHostName, Method=RequestMethod, Uri=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
  | where Url has_any (vulnPaths)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, DstHost=DstHostname, Method=HttpMethod, Uri=Url, Status=tostring(HttpStatusCode), UserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Source="ImWebSession")
| where Status startswith "2" or Status == "200"
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] node.exe bulk-deletes SillyTavern data\*\extensions\ directory (CVE-2026-44650 post-exploit) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the destructive side-effect of CVE-2026-44650: the SillyTavern node.exe process recursively deleting files under `data\<user>\extensions\`. The GHSA PoC shows `fs.promises.rm(extensionPath, { recursive: true })` against `data\default-user\extensions` — this surfaces as a tight burst of FileDeleted events from a single node.exe PID against files under that path. Hits even when no web logs are retained. Rationale: PoC body 'Extension has been deleted at data\default-user\extensions' confirms the destructive path pattern — `<basePath>\data\<user>\extensions\`. SillyTavern is a Node app so the deleting process is `node.exe`. Threshold of 5 deletions/minute distinguishes a wipe from the single-file legitimate uninstall (which removes one extension subdir, typically 1-3 files in one event). Cross-checked against related SillyTavern path-traversal CVEs (2026-34522/-34523/-34524) which describe the same parent directory layout. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-886q-f44j-h6wh • https://dailycve.com/sillytavern-unauthenticated-path-traversal-directory-deletion-cve-n-a-critical/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pkg/npm/sillytavern/CVE-2026-34524/
ATT&CKT1485 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileDeleted"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FolderPath has @"\data\" and FolderPath has @"\extensions\"
| summarize DeletedCount = count(),
            FirstDeletion = min(Timestamp),
            LastDeletion  = max(Timestamp),
            SampleFiles   = make_set(FileName, 25),
            SamplePaths   = make_set(FolderPath, 10)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where DeletedCount >= 5     // 5+ files removed under data\*\extensions\ in 1 minute = bulk wipe, not a single uninstall
| order by FirstDeletion desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileDeleted"
| where ActingProcessName endswith_cs "node.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith_cs "Node.exe"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\data\" and TargetFilePath has @"\extensions\"
| summarize DeletedCount = count(),
            FirstDeletion = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastDeletion  = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleFiles   = make_set(TargetFileName, 25),
            SamplePaths   = make_set(TargetFilePath, 10)
            by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where DeletedCount >= 5
| order by FirstDeletion desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:23 (@Image:*\\node.exe OR @Image:*\\Node.exe OR @Image:*\\NODE.EXE) (@TargetFilename:*\\data\\*\\extensions\\* OR @TargetFilename:*\\Data\\*\\Extensions\\*)

| DeletedCount >= 5
